sources.entry: Stage Manager - Replacement for Apple's Stage Manager written in Rust, with stages that survive restart and Ctrl-Option-1..9 switching. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon] ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]](https://github.com/eugene-tea/stage-manager)

summary.name: Stage Manager
summary.one_liner: A free, open-source macOS window manager written in Rust that replaces Apple's Stage Manager and keeps your stages after a restart.
use_cases: Keep separate sets of windows grouped into named stages on a Mac
Restore window groupings after restarting the Mac
Switch between window stages with keyboard shortcuts
Replace Apple's built-in Stage Manager with a customizable version
Set rules that place specific apps or windows in chosen stages
Edit window behaviour through a plain text config file
summary.what_it_does: Stage Manager is a macOS app that works like Apple's built-in Stage Manager, with a strip of cards showing your stages. Stages are kept across restarts in the same order. You can drop one card onto another to combine stages, and order cards manually or by Dock order. Holding Shift while opening an app places it in the current stage, and ⌃⌥1–9 switches stages or sends a window to one (enabled in Settings). Rules for new windows, the strip's appearance, and animations are set in a single plain text file, which Settings → Advanced explains how to edit.
notable: Stages persist across restarts, in the same order
Ctrl-Option-1..9 keyboard switching and sending windows to stages
Configured through one plain text file; Settings → Advanced explains editing
Open source and written in Rust
caveats: Requires macOS Accessibility permission to move windows
Screen Recording permission is optional and needed only for live window previews on cards
Makes a daily update check to GitHub unless turned off
